sentences.nl: In deze les gebruiken we de grammatica
sentences.en: In this lesson, we use the grammar.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• In deze les gebruiken we de grammatica  
  (In this lesson use we the grammar)

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the present tense of the verb "gebruiken" (to use).  
• "In deze les" means "in this lesson," with "deze" being a demonstrative pronoun meaning "this."  
• Word order: Dutch main clauses often follow the Subject-Verb-Object order, but here the prepositional phrase "in deze les" is placed at the beginning for emphasis.  
• Example phrases:  
  - "In dit boek leren we veel." (In this book we learn a lot.)  
  - "In die klas praten ze vaak." (In that class they talk often.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Tijdens de pauze eten we broodjes." (During the break we eat sandwiches.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)

sentences.nl: Vandaag belt Martin Marieke.
sentences.en: Today Martin calls Marieke.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Today calls Martin Marieke.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence follows a typical Dutch word order for simple sentences: [Time] [Verb] [Subject] [Object].  
• "Belt" is the third person singular present tense of "bellen" (to call). In Dutch, the verb typically comes second in main clauses.  
• "Vandaag" (today) is an adverb of time and often leads the sentence for emphasis or clarity.  
• Extra phrases:  
  - "Morgen komt de postbode langs." (Tomorrow the mailman comes by.)  
  - "Gisteren zag ik een film." (Yesterday I watched a movie.)  
  - "Elke dag eet zij een appel." (Every day she eats an apple.)

sentences.nl: Eh… waar is het telefoonnummer? — Ah… hier!
sentences.en: Eh... where is the phone number? — Ah... here!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Eh… waar is het telefoonnummer? — Ah… hier!  
(Um… where is the phone number? — Oh… here!)

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The word "waar" is used to ask about the location of something, similar to "where" in English.  
• "Het" is the definite article for neuter nouns in Dutch, used here with "telefoonnummer."  
• "Hier" means "here," indicating location.  
• The sentence uses ellipsis ("…") to indicate pauses typical in spoken language.

Extra phrases:  
• Waar is de supermarkt? (Where is the supermarket?)  
• Ah, daar is het boek. (Oh, there is the book.)  
• Eh, wat is je naam? (Um, what is your name?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Eh… waar ligt de sleutel? — Ah… daar!  
(Um… where is the key? — Oh… there!)

sentences.nl: Martin draait het nummer.
sentences.en: Martin plays the song.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Martin draait het nummer.  
  (Martin turns the number.)

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Draait" is the verb "draaien," meaning "to turn" or "to play" (a song). In this context, it means playing a song.  
• "Het nummer" means "the number" and refers to a song or track in this context.  
• Sentence structure: Subject (Martin) + Verb (draait) + Object (het nummer).

• Extra sentences:  
  - Zij draait de plaat. (She plays the record.)  
  - Ik draai de volumeknop. (I turn the volume knob.)  
  - De DJ draait de nieuwste hits. (The DJ plays the latest hits.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Lisa draait haar favoriete liedje. (Lisa plays her favorite song.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch, "nummer" is commonly used to refer to a song, especially in informal contexts. This usage reflects a broader trend where "nummer" is synonymous with "liedje" (song).

sentences.nl: Wat doe je? — Ik lees een boek.
sentences.en: What are you doing? — I am reading a book.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Wat doe je? — Ik lees een boek.  
  (What do you? — I read a book.)

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Wat doe je?" is a simple present tense question. In Dutch, questions often start with a question word followed by the verb and the subject.  
• "Ik lees een boek" uses the simple present tense to describe an action happening now. The verb "lees" is the first-person singular form of "lezen" (to read).  
• Example 1: "Wat eet je?" (What are you eating?)  
• Example 2: "Ik schrijf een brief." (I am writing a letter.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Wat zie je? — Ik zie een vogel." (What do you see? — I see a bird.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, reading is a popular pastime, with many people being members of public libraries and enjoying a wide range of Dutch and international literature.

sentences.nl: Welk boek? — Eh… een studieboek.

sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Which book? — Uh... a study book.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Welk" is an interrogative pronoun used to ask about a specific item or choice.  
• "Eh…" is an interjection often used to indicate hesitation or thinking.  
• "Een studieboek" is a noun phrase where "een" is an indefinite article and "studieboek" is a compound noun meaning "study book."

- Welke kleur wil je? (Which color do you want?)  
- Eh, ik weet het niet. (Uh, I don't know.)  
- Ze leest een kinderboek. (She is reading a children's book.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Welke film? — Eh… een documentaire. (Which movie? — Uh... a documentary.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)

sentences.nl: En wat doe je straks? — Straks ga ik naar de kapper.
sentences.en: And what are you doing later? — Later, I'm going to the hairdresser.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And what do you later? — Later go I to the hairdresser.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Straks" means "later" and refers to a near future time.  
• "Ga ik" is an example of inversion, where the subject ("ik") follows the verb ("ga"), commonly used in Dutch questions and after certain adverbs or conjunctions.  
• "Naar de kapper" uses the preposition "naar" which means "to" and is used for destinations.

Extra Examples:  
• "Straks ga ik boodschappen doen." (Later I will do the groceries.)  
• "En wat eet je straks?" (And what will you eat later?)  
• "Morgen ga ik naar de dokter." (Tomorrow I will go to the doctor.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Straks ga ik naar de supermarkt." (Later I will go to the supermarket.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Visiting the hairdresser is a common activity in the Netherlands, and appointments are usually made in advance. "Straks" is often used in casual conversations to refer to plans happening later the same day.

sentences.nl: Wat wil je? — Eh… Wat heb je? — Ik moet nog naar de markt.
sentences.en: What do you want? — Uh... What do you have? — I still have to go to the market.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Wat wil je? (What want you?)  
• Eh… Wat heb je? (Uh... What have you?)  
• Ik moet nog naar de markt. (I must still to the market.)

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Wat wil je?" uses inversion, a common structure in questions where the verb precedes the subject.  
• "Ik moet nog naar de markt." uses "moet" (must) to indicate necessity and "nog" to imply "still" or "yet."

• Example Sentences:  
  - Waar ga je? (Where are you going?)  
  - Ik moet nog eten. (I still need to eat.)  
  - Wat heb je nodig? (What do you need?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Hij moet nog zijn huiswerk maken. (He still has to do his homework.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
- Market visits are a common part of Dutch life, with many people shopping at local markets for fresh produce and other goods.

sentences.nl: Daarna neem ik de trein.
sentences.en: Then I take the train.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• After-that take I the train.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Daarna" is an adverb meaning "after that" and is used to indicate the sequence of events.  
• "Neem ik" is an example of subject-verb inversion, a common structure in Dutch when the sentence begins with an adverb or another element other than the subject.  
• "De trein" means "the train," and "de" is the definite article used for common gender nouns.

• Additional Examples:  
  - "Daarna eet ik lunch." (After that, I eat lunch.)  
  - "Daarna ga ik naar huis." (After that, I go home.)  
  - "Daarna bel ik je op." (After that, I will call you.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Daarna lees ik een boek. (After that, I read a book.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, public transportation, like trains, is a common and efficient way to travel between cities. Many Dutch people rely on the train system for daily commuting.

sentences.nl: Kom je meteen naar de markt? — Dat is goed.
sentences.en: Are you coming to the market right away? — That is fine.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Come you immediately to the market? — That is good.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Kom je" is an inversion of "je komt" due to the question form. In Dutch, questions often start with the verb.  
• "Meteen" means "immediately" or "right away," indicating promptness.  
• "Dat is goed" is a common phrase meaning "That's good" or "That's fine."  
• Examples:  
  - "Ga je morgen naar school?" (Are you going to school tomorrow?)  
  - "Dat is niet mogelijk." (That is not possible.)  
  - "Kom je vanavond eten?" (Are you coming for dinner tonight?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ga je meteen naar huis?" (Are you going home immediately?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Markets are popular in the Netherlands, often held weekly in towns and cities. They are not only for shopping but also for socializing.

sentences.nl: Welke markt? — De ‘Albert Cuyp’.
sentences.en: Which market? — The 'Albert Cuyp'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Which market? — The 'Albert Cuyp'.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Welke" is the interrogative pronoun for "which" and is used to ask about choices among a group.  
• "De Albert Cuyp" refers specifically to a well-known market in Amsterdam, named after the painter Albert Cuyp. The definite article "de" is used because it's a specific place.  
• Word order in Dutch questions typically places the interrogative word at the beginning, followed by the verb and subject.

• Extra phrases:  
  - Welke film wil je zien? (Which movie do you want to see?)  
  - Welke dag komt je vriendin aan? (Which day does your friend arrive?)  
  - Welke kleur vind je mooier? (Which color do you find prettier?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Welke winkel? — De ‘Bijenkorf’. (Which store? — The 'Bijenkorf'.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The Albert Cuyp market is one of the most famous street markets in the Netherlands, located in the De Pijp district of Amsterdam. It's known for its diverse offerings, from fresh produce to clothing and local delicacies.

sentences.nl: Waar is dat? — Dat is in ‘De Pijp’.
sentences.en: Where is that? — That is in 'De Pijp'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Where is that? — That is in 'The Pipe'.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence "Waar is dat?" uses the interrogative pronoun "waar" (where) followed by the verb "is" (is) and the pronoun "dat" (that), forming a simple question structure.  
• "Dat is in ‘De Pijp’" uses "dat" as a subject pronoun and "is" as the verb, followed by the preposition "in" to indicate location. "De Pijp" is a proper noun.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Waar is het station?" (Where is the station?)  
  - "Dat is in de buurt." (That is in the neighborhood.)  
  - "Waar zijn mijn sleutels?" (Where are my keys?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Waar is het restaurant? — Het is in het centrum." (Where is the restaurant? — It is in the center.)

## 4. Culture Note  
• "De Pijp" is a well-known neighborhood in Amsterdam, famous for its vibrant culture, the Albert Cuyp Market, and various restaurants and cafes.

sentences.nl: De Pijp? Wat is ‘De Pijp’? — De Pijp is een buurt in Amsterdam.
sentences.en: De Pijp? What is 'De Pijp'? — De Pijp is a neighborhood in Amsterdam.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The Pijp? What is 'The Pijp'? — The Pijp is a neighborhood in Amsterdam.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "De Pijp" is a proper noun referring to a specific neighborhood in Amsterdam. The definite article "de" is used for common gender nouns.  
• "Wat is 'De Pijp'?" is a simple interrogative sentence structure in Dutch; "Wat" means "What," "is" is the third person singular form of "to be," and "De Pijp" is the subject.  
• "is een buurt in Amsterdam" uses the structure [subject] + [to be] + [noun] + [prepositional phrase].  
• Example 1: "Wat is jouw naam?" (What is your name?)  
• Example 2: "De Jordaan is een ander buurt in Amsterdam." (The Jordaan is another neighborhood in Amsterdam.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "De Dam? Wat is 'De Dam'? — De Dam is een plein in Amsterdam." (The Dam? What is 'The Dam'? — The Dam is a square in Amsterdam.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• "De Pijp" is known for its vibrant atmosphere, multicultural population, and the famous Albert Cuyp Market, making it a popular spot for both locals and tourists.

sentences.nl: Hoeveel kilometer is dat van het station? — Van welk station? — Van het Centraal Station.
sentences.en: How many kilometers is that from the station? — From which station? — From the Central Station.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• How many kilometers is that from the station? — From which station? — From the Central Station.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hoeveel" means "how many" and is used here to ask about a quantity or distance.  
• "Is dat van het station?" uses "van" to indicate origin or starting point, similar to "from" in English.  
• "Welk" is a question word meaning "which," used for specifying one among several options.  
• "Het Centraal Station" is a specific noun phrase, referring to the main train station in a city.

Examples:  
– Hoeveel euro kost dat boek? (How many euros does that book cost?)  
– Welk huis is van jou? (Which house is yours?)  
– We vertrekken van het vliegveld. (We depart from the airport.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Hoeveel minuten duurt het om daarheen te lopen? (How many minutes does it take to walk there?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, train travel is very common, and most cities have a "Centraal Station," which is the main hub for trains and often located in the city center.

sentences.nl: Eh… Dat is ongeveer 2 kilometer lopen.
sentences.en: Eh... That is about a 2-kilometer walk.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Eh… That is approximately 2 kilometers walk.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dat is" is a simple present tense construction meaning "that is."  
• "Ongeveer" means "approximately" or "about," used to indicate an estimate.  
• "2 kilometer lopen" literally translates to "2 kilometers walk," where "lopen" is an infinitive verb meaning "to walk." Dutch often uses infinitive verbs in this way to describe activities or actions.

• Additional phrases:  
  - "Dat is ongeveer 10 minuten fietsen." (That is approximately 10 minutes cycling.)  
  - "Het is ongeveer een uur rijden." (It is approximately an hour driving.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Dat is ongeveer 3 uur varen. (That is approximately 3 hours sailing.)

sentences.en: Do you know all the question words from this lesson? — Do you understand the inversion? — If you don't understand it, then look again at lessons 7 and 8 of #dutchgrammar.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Know you all question words from this lesson? — Understand you the inversion? — If you it not understand, look then again lesson 7 and 8 of #dutchgrammar.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses inversion, which is common in Dutch questions. The verb precedes the subject ("Ken je" and "Begrijp je").  
• "Als je het niet begrijpt" uses a conditional clause starting with "als" (if), which is a common way to introduce conditions in Dutch.  
• The structure "kijk dan nog eens" is an imperative form, instructing someone to do something again.  
• Extra examples:  
  - "Ken je de regels van het spel?" (Do you know the rules of the game?)  
  - "Begrijp je waarom hij dat deed?" (Do you understand why he did that?)  
  - "Als het regent, blijf ik thuis." (If it rains, I stay at home.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ken je de namen van alle planten in de tuin?" (Do you know the names of all the plants in the garden?)
